# Qwen3.5 vision reference fixtures

What the Rust Qwen3.5 image preprocessing and M-RoPE position code must
reproduce, generated by Hugging Face's own implementation (no model weights):

- `*.png`: deterministic synthetic inputs (square, landscape, tall, tiny, odd).
- `reference.json`:
  - `processor`: the image processor constants (mean/std 0.5, bicubic,
    patch 16, temporal patch 2, merge 2, min/max pixels).
  - `images.<name>`: for the fast (torchvision) and slow (PIL) processors, the
    `grid_thw` and a summary of `pixel_values` (shape, sums, first/last 64
    values, every 1009th value), plus their max difference.
  - `prompts.<name>`: `input_ids`, image/video grids, the 3-row `position_ids`
    from `get_rope_index`, and `rope_delta`. Cases: one image, two images,
    multi-turn, a 4-frame video, text only.

The fast and slow processors agree on every grid and differ by at most one
8-bit level per value (0.0078 after normalisation), so that is the tolerance
for the Rust port's pixel values. Grids, token ids and positions must match
exactly. The 4-row layout the Qwen3.5 language model takes adds row 0 = token
index (GenAI `qwen3_5/classes.cpp`); these fixtures hold HF's 3 rows.

Regenerate with `tools/vlm_fixtures/gen_qwen35_fixtures.py` (transformers
5.14.1, torch 2.14.1, torchvision 0.29.1; versions are recorded in the JSON)
against a Qwen3.5/3.6 export directory, e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-int4-ov.
